title: rootless: --pids-limit=-1/0 sets cgroup pids.max=1 instead of unlimited
body:
## Description

`podman run --pids-limit=-1` (and `--pids-limit=0`) are documented/intended to mean "unlimited" pids for the container. Instead, on a rootless setup with cgroup v2 + the systemd cgroup manager, the container's cgroup ends up with `pids.max` literally set to `1` — meaning the container can host exactly one process. Any attempt to fork a second process inside the container fails immediately with `Resource temporarily unavailable`.

Omitting `--pids-limit` entirely (falls back to the `containers.conf` default of 2048) or passing any explicit positive number works correctly.

This reproduces both with and without `--privileged`, so it isn't specific to privileged mode.

## Steps to reproduce

```console
$ podman run -d --rm --pids-limit=-1 docker.io/library/alpine:latest sleep 30
<cid>

$ podman exec <cid> sh -c 'sh -c "echo forked-ok"'
sh: can't fork: Resource temporarily unavailable

$ podman inspect <cid> --format '{{.State.Pid}}'
<pid>
$ awk -F: '{print $3}' /proc/<pid>/cgroup
/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/user.slice/libpod-<cid>.scope
$ cat /sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/user.slice/libpod-<cid>.scope/pids.max
1
```

Compare with a positive limit, which behaves correctly:

```console
$ podman run -d --rm --pids-limit=4096 docker.io/library/alpine:latest sleep 30
<cid>
$ podman exec <cid> sh -c 'sh -c "echo forked-ok"'
forked-ok
$ cat /sys/fs/cgroup/.../libpod-<cid>.scope/pids.max
4096
```

And with the flag omitted (default):

```console
$ podman run -d --rm docker.io/library/alpine:latest sleep 30
$ cat /sys/fs/cgroup/.../libpod-<cid>.scope/pids.max
2048
```

## Full table

| `--pids-limit` value | resulting cgroup `pids.max` | fork works inside container? |
|---|---|---|
| (omitted) | `2048` | yes |
| `-1` | `1` | **no** |
| `0` | `1` | **no** |
| `4096` | `4096` | yes |

## Expected behavior

`--pids-limit=-1` (and per the docs, `0`) should result in `pids.max` being set to `max` (unlimited), not `1`.

## Environment

```
$ podman version
Client:       Podman Engine
Version:      4.9.3
API Version:  4.9.3
Go Version:   go1.22.2
OS/Arch:      linux/amd64

$ podman info --format '{{.Host.OCIRuntime.Name}} {{.Host.OCIRuntime.Version}}'
runc runc version 1.4.3
commit: v1.4.3-0-gbb14dabe
spec: 1.3.0

$ podman info --format 'CgroupVersion={{.Host.CgroupsVersion}} CgroupManager={{.Host.CgroupManager}}'
CgroupVersion=v2 CgroupManager=systemd

$ cat /etc/os-release
NAME="Linux Mint"
VERSION="22.3 (Zena)"

$ uname -r
6.17.0-1030-oem
```

Rootless podman, invoked directly (`podman run ...`), no extra wrapping beyond a plain user session (no container manager, no Docker-compat shim).

## Additional context

This silently breaks any workload that relies on `--pids-limit=-1`/`0` meaning "unlimited" — in our case, a dev-container entrypoint using `dumb-init` as PID 1 failed at its very first `fork()` with `[dumb-init] Unable to fork. Exiting.`, which took some digging to trace back to the cgroup `pids.max=1`. Related but distinct from #11782 (which was about `-1` being rejected outright) and #13891 (which is the opposite failure — the limit being silently *ignored*, `pids.max` staying `max`, in rootless mode). Here the flag is accepted and *does* take effect, just with the wrong numeric value.

comments.body:
We only support the latest version and it works already there.
```
$ podman run --rm --pids-limit=-1 quay.io/libpod/testimage:20241011 cat /sys/fs/cgroup/pids.max
max
$ podman run --rm --pids-limit=0 quay.io/libpod/testimage:20241011 cat /sys/fs/cgroup/pids.max
max
$ podman run --rm --pids-limit=1 quay.io/libpod/testimage:20241011 cat /sys/fs/cgroup/pids.max
1
$ podman run --rm --pids-limit=5 quay.io/libpod/testimage:20241011 cat /sys/fs/cgroup/pids.max
5
$ podman run --rm  quay.io/libpod/testimage:20241011 cat /sys/fs/cgroup/pids.max
2048
```
